claims.statement: Newly created secrets become available on new codespace creation or restart; using a newly created hosted secret in a running instance requires stopping and restarting that instance. Secret creation alone is not evidence of live propagation, authorized access or successful application use. The stopping procedure remains separate; no secret or runtime changed.

The incomplete introductory sentence belongs to a tutorial using the web editor to open a project and modify predefined dev container configuration, with later applicability to the user's repository through web or desktop editors. Tutorial learning intent is not a verified setup, universal policy or permission to execute installation; the introduction link remains separate.

GPG verification and Settings Sync share a trusted-repository list, so with both features enabled a selected GPG-trusted repository also gets sync and newly trusting for sync enables GPG verification for that repository. The feature enable/disable switches remain independent. The source recommends replacing all-repository GPG trust with a selected trusted list, not certifying every selected repository as safe. The linked security section, actual trust scope and live propagation remain separate.

Settings Sync can share the context-defined settings across web and desktop codespaces. The web client defaults to disabled and must enable sync for pushing/pulling changes. This general default must be read with the trusted-repository/both-features qualifiers in DOCS-CODESPACESTRUSTSYNC-003 rather than treated as proof of a particular instance's current state. The antecedent settings scope and linked preference article remain separate; no synchronization changed.
